Question Choices: A rectangle has area = 56 square units. One side is 7 units. What is the other side?
Hints: Divide area by the known side length. The result is a length.
Solution: Divide area by the known side: 56 divided by 7 = 8 units. Check: 7 x 8 = 56. A side length uses linear units.

Question Choices: A rectangle is split into two smaller rectangles. One has area 45, the other 120. What is the total area? All areas are in square units; the parts do not overlap.
Hints: Add the areas of the separate parts, using the same square units.
Solution: Add the areas of the parts, counting each part once: 45 + 120 = 165 square units.

Question Choices: A large rectangle is made from two rectangles: Area of rectangle A is 67. Area of rectangle B is 94. What is the total area? All areas are in square units; the parts do not overlap.
Hints: Add the areas of the separate parts, using the same square units.
Solution: Add the areas of the parts, counting each part once: 67 + 94 = 161 square units.

Question Choices: Two lots cost the same price. Lot A area = 2,500 square meters (m^2). Lot B area = 2,000 square meters (m^2). Based on area alone, which lot gives more land for the same price? : A B
Hints: At the same price, compare the areas using matching units.
Solution: At the same price, 2500 > 2000. Lot A gives 500 square metres more land.
